question: The amount on a sum of ₹5,000 at 20% per annum compound interest, compounded annually, in 2 years, will be:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective rate of compound interest for 2 years at 20% p.a. = 20 + 20 + (20 × 20) ÷ 100 = 44%.

Total amount = 100% (Principal) + 44% (Interest) = 144% of Principal.

Amount = 144% of 5000 = (144 ÷ 100) × 5000 = 144 × 50 = 7200.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹5,000

Rate (R) = 20% p.a.

Time (T) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P × (1 + R ÷ 100)T

 
 
 

 
 

 
 
• 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Year 0
 Year 1
 Year 2
 
 ₹5000
 ₹6000
 A = ?
 
 
 

 

 
 
 +20%
 +20%

**Calculations:**

⇒ A = 5000 × (1 + 20 ÷ 100)²

⇒ A = 5000 × (1 + 1 ÷ 5)²

⇒ A = 5000 × (6 ÷ 5)²

⇒ A = 5000 × (36 ÷ 25)

⇒ A = 200 × 36

⇒ A = 7200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate of CI

For 2 years, the effective compound interest rate can be calculated using the formula: Rₑffₑ꜀ₜᵢvₑ = X + Y + (X × Y) ÷ 100.

Difference between CI and SI

For 2 years, the exact difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest on a principal P is given by: Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)².

Half-Yearly Compounding

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the rate of interest becomes half (R ÷ 2) and the time period is doubled (2 × T).
